title: Half the world’s leaders should be women, says Iceland’s former PM
gist: A short WEF video blurb in which Iceland's former PM Katrín Jakobsdóttir argues that women are half the global workforce but hold only a third of corporate leadership roles, framing this as a decision-quality problem rather than only an equity one, with childcare, parental leave and board hiring practices as the binding constraints. The same page frames WEF's upcoming editorial month around the claim that scaling, not inventing, is the bottleneck for AI, quantum and biotech.

insights.claim: Women make up half the global workforce but hold only about one third of corporate leadership roles, a gap that persists two decades into systematic gender-parity tracking.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: The leadership share, not labour-force participation, is the metric that still has room to move — watch board and C-suite composition disclosures rather than headline employment data for signs of change.
insights.quote: Women make up half the global workforce, but hold only a third of corporate leadership roles.
insights.locator: Women make up half the global workforce

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum has published a report titled 'Closing the Gender Gap in Senior Leadership' examining how to raise female representation at senior levels, signalling institutional attention on the senior tier specifically rather than overall workforce parity.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
entities: Closing the Gender Gap in Senior Leadership
Centre for the New Economy and Society
insights.so_what: Institutional benchmarking of senior-leadership composition tends to precede investor and regulator pressure on disclosure — useful as a leading indicator for governance-screen mandates.
insights.locator: A new World Economic Forum report

themes.theme: Diversity as decision quality, not equity

insights.claim: Katrín Jakobsdóttir argues the under-representation of women in leadership is not primarily an equity issue but a missed opportunity for better decision-making, because diverse leadership teams consistently outperform homogeneous ones.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reframes board diversity from a compliance cost to a performance input — the argument an allocator would need to make diversity a return driver rather than an ESG screen.
insights.quote: this isn't just an equity issue: it's a missed opportunity for better decision-making, since diverse leadership teams consistently outperform homogeneous ones
insights.locator: Iceland's former PM Katrín Jakobsdóttir argues

insights.claim: A former head of government of Iceland is the one making the economic-performance case for gender-balanced leadership, tying the argument to a country that has pushed parity policy furthest rather than to corporate advocacy.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Policy-side advocates carry more weight than corporate DEI functions in shaping mandatory board rules — relevant to jurisdictions considering quota legislation.
insights.locator: Iceland's former PM Katrín Jakobsdóttir argues

themes.theme: Childcare, leave and board hiring as the binding constraints

insights.claim: The practical barriers keeping capable people out of leadership are identified as childcare provision, parental leave policy and board hiring practices — concrete policy and process levers rather than attitudes or pipeline supply.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Locates the fix in fiscal and governance policy, so changes in state childcare funding or board-nomination rules are the actionable triggers to watch, not corporate diversity pledges.
insights.quote: the practical barriers from childcare and parental leave policy to board hiring practices that keep capable people out of leadership
insights.locator: Here, Jakobsdóttir unpacks the practical barriers

insights.claim: Despite an AI boom, accelerating quantum breakthroughs and billions flowing into biotech, the measurable real-world impact of these technologies has not yet arrived — innovation is only the beginning and the real challenge is scaling what works.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Implies the durable value accrues to deployment and scaling capacity rather than to invention — a bias toward adoption-layer and industrial-integration plays over pure research-stage exposure.
insights.quote: AI is booming. Quantum breakthroughs are accelerating. Billions are pouring into biotech. So why isn’t the world feeling the impact yet?
insights.locator: AI is booming. Quantum breakthroughs are accelerating.

insights.claim: The leadership-diversity argument is placed inside an editorial programme about turning technological breakthroughs into real-world progress, implicitly connecting who makes decisions to whether new technologies actually get scaled into industries and economies.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
entities: Centre for the New Economy and Society
insights.so_what: If leadership composition is being framed as a scaling input for frontier tech, expect diversity metrics to migrate from ESG reporting into operational and talent due diligence.
